chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Why he stayed twenty years; liking and missing the road
summary: Raises and habit kept him with Basie until gallstones; he describes the pleasures and adjustments of road life.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Why did you stay so long? Were you (inaudible)?
Well, sometimes it was -- sometimes I was enjoying myself, sometimes I wasn't. Everytime I'd go to

leave, if I'd get a little bit raise, I'd stay a little bit longer, and after a while, it seemed to be a part of my life to be out there. It just seemed to be natural for me to be out there after I'd been there for ten, 12 years. I would have probably have felt strange being anywhere else other than that. So, I just stayed on and on and on. Had to come home and get my gallstones taken out, so that was the end of that.

Yes and no. Sometimes, it was nice. You meet nice people. I think the world really consists of the nice people that you meet and the bad people that you meet, if there is such a thing as a bad person. It got to the place where you could look forward to going to certain places because you knew that you were going to meet certain people when you got there and enjoy certain niceties that came along with it, you know? You learned to meet nice people and people that respected you for what you were.

After you made the circuit a couple of times, you were always at the place where you were able to define between who was the phony and who wasn't the phony. So, you could enjoy yourself if you wanted to and if you didn't, you just took it as another night's work.
Did you ever get restless, staying in one spot? Did you miss the change (inaudible)?
When I first came home, after a while, I

was just a little bit restless. I missed the routine of doing certain things and you get tied into routines in any phase of life and that's what it was, more than anything else. My sleeping hours were different and my eating hours were different, what I ate was different and where I slept was different. I had to get accustomed to sleeping in my own bed, you know? Those things are a winding-down process and it's not really bad. But it's uncomfortable at times, until you get yourself regimented to what it is.
